first.rationale: Activation is down 6% QoQ and onboarding completion down 4% QoQ. Memory_91 showed that activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and first meaningful action. This directly addresses the activation decline without the retention risk of promotional_pricing (memory_73) or the narrow applicability of referral_incentives (memory_57, best for established customers). Memory_31 showed onboarding simplification worked, but memory_86 indicates shortening onboarding has already been implemented. Activation messaging is a complementary lever that can re-engage accounts during their critical early period. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is valuable but doesn't address the SMB activation problem or the competitive pricing pressure. Verifying memory_31 and memory_91 will confirm the durability and implementation details of both onboarding simplification and activation messaging approaches before committing.

final.rationale: Archive verification confirms activation_messaging is the optimal choice. Memory_91 delivered +6% activation with +1% retention lift and no downside risk. Memory_31 shows signup simplification worked (+9% activation) but is already implemented (per memory_86). Activation messaging directly addresses the current 6% QoQ activation decline without the retention penalty of promotional_pricing (memory_73: -30-day retention despite revenue lift) or the narrow applicability of referral incentives to established customers only. The competitive pricing pressure from the competitor is best defended through superior activation and time-to-value, not price matching. Activation messaging can be deployed quickly across self-serve and SMB cohorts to re-engage accounts in their critical first week. Standard experiment scale allows measurement across segments while limiting downside exposure.
